evidence.text: Memory-cost inflation is a gross-margin and capex risk. TrendForce forecast Q3 2026 server DRAM contract prices up 13-18% q/q, after 53-58% in Q2, with buyers without long-term agreements bearing most of it. Fastly guided capex to 10-12% of revenue (about 5% in 2025), said it is 'closely monitoring supply chain dynamics particularly regarding memory components', and guided gross margin to 65% ±50bp. F5 guided its FY27 gross margin lower on higher component costs on 2026-10-28.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin was a record 65.8%, 180bp above the guide, and the stock still fell 12.9%. In April 2026 a Craig-Hallum downgrade citing capex and memory costs coincided with a -14% day (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-fastly-stock-plunged-14-tuesday).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has flagged but not quantified. If it were priced, the FY FCF guide of $40-50m would already be cut in consensus, and no source shows that. The size is small because it is a proxy and the cost runs mostly through depreciation, so it reaches COGS with a lag.
evidence.independence: F5's component-cost margin guide (https://www.trefis.com/stock/ffiv/articles/621359/what-just-happened-to-ffiv-stock/2026-10-29) is a direct counterparty-class confirmation. evidence.text: Management has twice said it recognised only part of the favourable 2026 market-morbidity and risk-adjustment signal. On Q1 (2026-05-06) Bertolini said claims were better than expected but 'we have not booked all of that', and RA reserves were still set on pricing morbidity. On Q2 (2026-08-06) CFO Blackley said Oscar recognised 'only a small portion' of the favourability in the first 2026 market report. Each quarter's beat has since been followed by a raised operating guide: $250-450m to $500-700m in August, then to $600-800m on 2026-09-16. A further release of that held-back accrual would land on Q3 earnings from operations against a consensus of about -$63m EBIT and -$0.22 EPS, and could take the FY guide above $600-800m (the Q3 call is the next venue).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat and raise: Q1 2026 (EPS $2.07, guide reaffirmed with a 'meet or exceed' stance) bought +10.59%. Q2 2026 (EPS $1.10 vs $0.43, operating guide raised $250m) spiked more than 20% pre-market and closed -11.86% on H2 churn worries. The 2026-09-16 investor-day raise of +$100m bought about +2.4%. Q3 2025 beat: -2.76%. Beats on this line pay about half the time.
evidence.why_not_priced: The size of the held-back accrual was never quantified, so consensus cannot model it. The iTiger preview of 2026-10-29 has consensus at a Q3 loss of -$0.22 and quotes UBS saying in-quarter upside is limited because the guide already embeds favourable utilisation. If the market had priced a further release, Q3 EPS estimates would sit near breakeven rather than at a loss and the sell-side mix would not read mostly bearish. Part of it is probably in the 16.7% five-day run-up and the call-bid skew, which is why this is sized well under the implied move.

The unpriced part is that consensus revenue still sits at the top of what the unchanged revenue guide implies. If the market had marked revenue to the churn guidance, Q3 revenue estimates would cluster near $4.6bn, not $4.72-4.82bn. The offset is that peer Centene's marketplace members fell only 2.6% in Q3 (3.49m to 3.40m), which argues the attrition was milder than feared.
